priceSnapshot.source: OKX Public API v5 /market/candles?bar=1m, in-progress bar stamped 2026-09-18T14:16:00Z, read via server-side fetch. Cross-checked against the OKX 15m in-progress bar at 80,514.9 and against TradingEconomics BTCUSD at 80,150 (+4.89 percent, Sep/18).
priceSnapshot.note: THE BREAKOUT HAPPENED AND IT WAS VIOLENT. Price is 80,501.1, up 5.34 percent on the 76,419.2 UTC day open and up 3,886.9 points and 5.07 percent on the 76,614.2 midday handover. The 77,167.3 add gate the midday session raised did not merely fire - it was cleared and left behind. The move was not linear: the tape ground from 76,258.2 to 78,473.5 through the Asia and London sessions, spent four hours coiling between 77,980 and 78,473, then went vertical in the 13:00 UTC hour, opening 78,050 and printing 80,515.8 - a 2,465.8-point, 3.16 percent hour on 1,422 BTC, the heaviest hourly volume in the series. It has since extended to a 80,632.2 session high. A DATA-INTEGRITY NOTE THAT MATTERS: the OKX proxy served this run cached responses of wildly different ages - /public/time returned a stamp 13.7 hours old, /market/ticker returned 78,016.5 stamped 12:09 UTC, Kraken returned 78,290.7 and Coinbase 77,978.2 stamped 08:53 UTC. Those were all discarded as stale. The 80,501.1 mark is corroborated three ways: the 1m and 15m candle series agree, the realized-liquidation tape shows fills at 80,314 to 80,574 stamped 14:05 UTC, and TradingEconomics independently prints 80,150 up 4.89 percent. Every number in this report is tagged with the timestamp of the feed it came from.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below 78,473.5. This replaces the 76,050.4 gate that stood for four sessions and never fired - it is now 4,242.6 points below the mark and has stopped being a decision level. 78,473.5 is yesterday's session ceiling and the top of the four-hour coil that preceded the vertical hour; it is the price the market has to hold for the breakout to be a breakout rather than a spike. It sits 2,027.6 points under the mark, which is 3.90 times the 519.50-point 1H ATR, so this is a wide gate by design: after a 3.16 percent hour the noise band is enormous and a tight level would be stopped out by the first mean-reversion candle. A settled close below it means the squeeze fully retraced and the 80,000 handle was a liquidity event, not a repricing.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above the 80,632.2 session high. Be honest about what this level is for: it is a continuation confirmation, not an invitation to chase. The 1H RSI14 is 85.69 and the 15m RSI14 is 87.28, both the most stretched readings in this series, and the 80,400 to 80,500 short-liquidation shelf that fuelled the last leg has already been consumed - 1,281,474 USD of shorts were carried out in seven minutes and that fuel does not regenerate. The preferred add is NOT this level but a controlled pullback into 78,473.5 to 79,000 that holds on a settled close, which would convert the breakout into a base. This desk is taking profit into the spike rather than adding to it, and the add gate is published for completeness and for the sessions that follow.

decisionBox.changed: Everything changed. Bias moves from RANGE with a bullish tilt to outright BULLISH, the first non-range print in this series for over a week. Position moves from ADD to TAKE_PROFIT - not because the thesis broke but because it worked faster than the plan assumed and the wallet is 98 percent concentrated in spot with 4.02 USDT of cash. The reduce gate moves up 2,423.1 points from 76,050.4 to 78,473.5; the add gate moves up 3,464.9 points from 77,167.3 to 80,632.2. Confidence rises from 5.75 to 6.50 - the structural evidence is the strongest it has been, but a vertical squeeze into RSI 86 caps how much confidence a 5 percent day can earn. Probabilities move 40/39/21 to 50/29/21. ORDERING CAVEAT: this session ran at 09:20 COT, seven hours and twenty minutes late and fifteen minutes AFTER the 09:05 morning session, which published its own gates at 79,250.0 reduce and 80,555.4 add from an independent data pull. Both sets are defensible - this one is deliberately wider because a 3.16 percent hour makes tight gates meaningless - but morning's are the later read and the operative ones for the remainder of the day.

liquidation.note: Highest short-liquidation prints on the tape, 81,755 USD across the 80,550-80,600 bucket. Thin relative to the shelf below it, which is the point: the heavy fuel was spent lower and what remains above is light.
354,605 USD of short liquidations in the 80,450-80,500 bucket, including a single 206.82-contract fill. Sits 5.9 points under the mark, so price is balanced directly on top of it.

The largest cluster on the tape by a wide margin: 800,562 USD in the 80,400-80,450 bucket, of which a SINGLE fill of 916.97 contracts at 80,406.8 accounts for roughly 737,000 USD. This one print is the engine of the whole move. It is now the first real shelf beneath the market - already consumed, so it offers support by structure rather than by resting orders.

172,807 USD of LONG liquidations in the 79,900-79,950 bucket at 13:58 UTC - the late longs who bought the first leg and were shaken out minutes before the vertical hour. A clean marker of where impatient leverage sat.

liquidityMagnet.source: OKX /api/v5/public/liquidation-orders?instType=SWAP&uly=BTC-USDT&state=filled, 100 most recent fills covering 13:58:19 to 14:05:32 UTC, contract size 0.01 BTC, bucketed to 50 points; plus /api/v5/rubik/stat/contracts/long-short-account-ratio (fresh, 13:00 UTC).
liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is UP on weight but the reading carries a large caveat. Shorts were carried out 1,281,474 USD against 200,736 USD of longs, a 6.38-to-1 ratio, and every one of those fills is a forced buy. But this is a REALIZED tape spanning seven minutes, not a forward heatmap, and both clusters have already been visited and consumed. The honest statement is that the pull WAS violently up and the fuel that produced it is now spent; what sits above 80,632 is unmeasured. The forward map would need a keyed CoinGlass source - the free OKX feed gives realized fills only, and the browser fallback was unavailable this run.

etfFlows.note: THE BID CAME BACK. Farside Investors US spot Bitcoin ETF tape, read 2026-09-18 with the page self-stamping today's date. 17 September printed PLUS 159.5 million - IBIT plus 183.7, FBTC minus 16.6, HODL minus 7.6 - ending the two-day bleed and reversing the single most bearish input in the previous four reports. The run now reads 11 Sep minus 13.2, 14 Sep plus 159.9, 15 Sep minus 450.4, 16 Sep minus 295.9, 17 Sep plus 159.5. streakDays is plus 1. 18 September is unreported - every issuer column is a dash and the total renders 0.0 - so today's flow, which will print tonight, is the single most important number the endday session will have. The sequencing is what convinces: the regulated bid turned positive on Thursday and price went vertical on Friday. Cumulative since 08 September is now minus 889.6 million, still negative, but the marginal direction has flipped.

liquidations.note: READ THE TIMESTAMPS: this session ran roughly seven hours late and therefore AFTER the 2026-09-18 morning session, so these figures are the TAIL of the cascade morning captured, not a separate event. Own measurement: 1,281,474 USD of shorts force-covered against 200,736 USD of longs, 6.38 to 1, from the 100 most recent fills spanning 13:58:19 to 14:05:32 UTC. That is a seven-minute window and NOT a 24-hour total. Compare it with what the morning session measured eleven minutes earlier over 13:44:25 to 13:55:30 UTC - 16,338,561 USD of shorts against 425,179 USD of longs across 800 saturated fills, a 38.4-to-1 skew. The drop from 38.4-to-1 to 6.38-to-1 and from 16.3 million to 1.28 million is the single most useful thing in this section: the ignition is over and the short fuel is largely burned. Price is still making highs on far less forced buying, which is what a squeeze looks like as it matures into either a base or a fade. The skew field carries the long-short ACCOUNT ratio at 1.37 as of the 13:00 UTC bucket - 1.70 at 00:00 UTC, then 1.66, 1.62, 1.56, 1.51, 1.46, 1.39, 1.37, falling for thirteen straight hours while price rose 4,200 points. Accounts kept REDUCING net long exposure into the rally, an unloved breakout rather than a crowded one. OPEN INTEREST is the correction this session has to make: the OKX endpoint returned 2,185,826,806 USD to this run stamped 2026-09-18T00:34:57Z, 13.7 hours stale and entirely pre-breakout, so it was DISCARDED. The value published here, 2,323,868,439.51 USD, is the fresh read taken by the 2026-09-18 morning session at 09:05 COT and is used with attribution rather than re-measured. On that figure open interest is up 5.78 percent against the 2,196,790,542 handover while price rose 4.83 percent, so the move WAS partly built on new leverage - the question this session initially called untestable is in fact answered, and answered unfavourably. Funding likewise: the stale 0.0001 print from 2026-09-17T16:52:10Z was discarded in favour of morning's plus 0.00663 percent - positive, longs paying, but roughly a tenth of what a crowded top reads, with the perpetual at a 29.4-point DISCOUNT to index.

This matches the figure the 2026-09-18 morning session published from the same resolved set.
calibration.note: The cleanest calibration result in this series. The midday 77,167.3 ADD gate FIRED and then some - price cleared it by 3,333.8 points and never looked back, and the 13:00 UTC hour alone traded 2,465.8 points. The 76,050.4 reduce gate did NOT fire; the lowest print since the handover was 76,258.2, leaving 207.8 points of clearance on price and far more on a settled-close basis. The 74,955.5 invalidation was never threatened. Directionally midday published RANGE with a BULLISH tilt at 40 bull against 21 bear and price is 5.07 percent higher, so the call was right in sign and badly understated in magnitude - a 5 percent day inside a RANGE bias is a miss on regime even when the direction is right, and that is the lesson being booked. Discretionary: midday BOUGHT a 7.50 USDT spot tranche at 76,614.2 and spot marks 80,501.1, so that tranche is 3,886.9 points onside, roughly plus 0.38 USDT on a 7.50 slice. Acting helped, decisively. The 13 September flush rule is RETIRED here rather than carried forward, and it is retired having FAILED its eleventh and final test. The liquidation leg passes at 6.38-to-1 shorts and the account-ratio leg passes at 1.37 and falling, but the open-interest leg fails again and decisively: 2,323,868,439 USD against the 2,196,790,542 handover, up 5.78 percent while price rose 4.83. This session's own OI fetch came back 13.7 hours stale and pre-breakout and was discarded in favour of the morning session's fresh read - so the leg is testable after all, and the honest verdict is failure, not a technicality. Eleven tests, no clean pass, and 74,955.5 was never confirmed as a flush low. The rule was written to time a range low; the range is gone and the market is 5,545.6 points above that level, so it stops being carried. ONE PROCESS NOTE FOR THE RECORD: this midnight session executed at 09:20 COT, roughly seven hours and twenty minutes after its 02:00 slot and fifteen minutes AFTER the 09:05 morning session. The two reports were produced independently from separate data pulls, which is why their gates differ - and where they differ, morning's are the later and operative ones. The ledger handover message written by this run is addressed to morning and should be read by midday instead.
